gen_risks.description: Low market uptake of the new Sustainability‑Linked Loan (SLL) and Green Loan (GL) products may limit financing volumes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement step‑down pricing incentives, conduct targeted outreach to mid‑caps and SMEs, and monitor uptake to adjust incentives quickly.
gen_risks.evidence: Market for sustainable finance instruments remains nascent and concentrated among large corporations (Section B.7).

gen_risks.description: Credit risk of SME and mid‑cap borrowers due to weak collateral and high information asymmetry.
gen_risks.mitigation: Require minimum co‑financing, use independent validation of sustainability plans, and apply risk‑adjusted pricing margins.
gen_risks.evidence: Limited collateral recovery, information asymmetries, and short‑term funding structures constrain SME financing (Section B.13‑B.15).

gen_risks.description: Insufficient Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) capacity may delay loan approvals and affect ESG compliance.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide dedicated MRV training to PFIs and BEs, fund initial MRV costs, and develop standardized digital tools.
gen_risks.evidence: Limited availability of credible MRV systems constrains lenders’ capacity (Section B.15).

gen_risks.description: Risk of greenwashing if sustainability plans are not rigorously validated.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate ex‑ante validation and ex‑post verification by independent entities for all SLL/GL projects.
gen_risks.evidence: To mitigate the risk of greenwashing, targets will be subject to ex‑ante validation and ex‑post verification (Section D.1a).

gen_risks.description: Women‑owned firms may be under‑represented among loan beneficiaries, limiting gender impact goals.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set explicit women‑inclusive eligibility criteria, track gender metrics, and run targeted outreach campaigns.
gen_risks.evidence: Women‑owned firms have lower access to formal financing (Section B.20‑B.21).

gen_risks.description: Physical climate risks (heatwaves, floods) could impair beneficiary operations and loan repayment.
gen_risks.mitigation: Integrate climate‑risk assessments into loan underwriting and promote resilience‑enhancing technologies.
gen_risks.evidence: Extreme weather raises loan delinquency rates among Mexican firms (Section B.19).

gen_risks.description: Delay in adopting the Project Operations Manual and Sustainable Finance Framework could postpone disbursements.
gen_risks.mitigation: Set interim milestones, monitor adoption progress, and provide technical assistance to expedite approvals.
gen_risks.evidence: Effectiveness requires adoption of the POM and Sustainable Finance Framework (Conditions section).

gen_risks.description: Participating Financial Institutions (PFIs) may lack expertise to appraise and monitor green loans.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deliver capacity‑building TA to PFIs on green‑loan underwriting, risk assessment, and monitoring tools.
gen_risks.evidence: Mexican financial institutions are limited in capacity to design, originate, appraise and monitor green loans (Section B.15).

gen_risks.description: Non‑compliance with environmental and social standards could trigger legal or reputational penalties.
gen_risks.mitigation: Embed strict ESMS clauses in loan agreements, conduct bi‑annual E&S reporting, and audit high‑risk borrowers.
gen_risks.evidence: E&S risk is Substantial; compliance clauses will be incorporated into loan agreements (Section C.3).

gen_risks.description: Currency fluctuations may affect the real cost of MXN‑denominated loans for borrowers and NAFIN.
gen_risks.mitigation: NAFIN to hedge FX exposure via swaps and monitor exchange‑rate movements regularly.
gen_risks.evidence: NAFIN will manage the FX risk on its own balance sheet using Mexico’s currency swap market (Section D.31).

gen_risks.description: Strict eligibility and retroactive‑financing limits could cause cash‑flow gaps for early‑stage projects.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide clear guidance on eligible pre‑signature expenditures and allow timely advance requests within the $40 M cap.
gen_risks.evidence: Withdrawals prior to Signature Date limited to $40 M for eligible expenditures (Disbursement section).

gen_risks.description: Reliance on legacy financial systems may cause reporting delays and errors.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement interim data‑reconciliation procedures, conduct regular internal audits, and plan gradual digitalization.
gen_risks.evidence: Residual FM risk moderate due to reliance on legacy information systems (Section B.54).

gen_risks.description: Grievance Redress Service may be under‑utilized, leading to unresolved stakeholder complaints.
gen_risks.mitigation: Promote the GRS through the Stakeholder Engagement Plan, set response‑time targets, and monitor complaint logs.
gen_risks.evidence: SEP includes a Grievance Redress Mechanism to receive and address Project‑related complaints (Section C.60).

gen_risks.description: Targeted private capital mobilization of US$89 M may not be achieved, limiting leverage effect.
gen_risks.mitigation: Activate co‑financing requirements, engage anchor companies early, and showcase pilot successes to attract investors.
gen_risks.evidence: Project will help mobilize an estimated US$89 M in private capital (Section D.28).

gen_risks.description: Beneficiary firms may lack technical capacity to implement renewable or energy‑efficiency technologies.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide feasibility studies, technical assistance, and subsidized MRV support for high‑impact technologies.
gen_risks.evidence: Most firms lack capacity to measure emissions, implement energy‑use systems, or comply with reporting frameworks (Section B.15‑B.16).

gt_risks.description: The Project channels financing to SMEs/mid-caps via NAFIN through Green Loans (GLs) and Sustainability-Linked Loans (SLLs). For GLs, E&S risk is limited (resources go to a pre-screened positive list), but SLLs operate as corporate loans, making site-specific impacts harder to trace and creating risk around traceability of environmental outcomes and possible greenwashing if sustainability targets are weak or under-monitored.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN prepared an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) summary covering main E&S risks by key sector, disclosed at appraisal.

gt_risks.description: Introduction of new financial instruments (notably SLLs) not currently deployed in Mexico, which may lack sufficient demand, drives the technical design risk rating.
gt_risks.mitigation: Substantial TA to NAFIN, PFIs, and beneficiary enterprises (BEs) to support instrument design/deployment; GFPP grant to advance instrument design during preparation; NAFIN required to prepare and adopt a Sustainable Finance Framework (covering SLLs and GLs) acceptable to the Bank prior to effectiveness; draw on global best practices from comparable SLL facilities; Bank hands-on support during initial deployment.

gt_risks.description: The Project requires close coordination and participation of several stakeholders: different units within NAFIN, participating financial institutions (PFIs), beneficiary enterprises, and large anchor companies heading the green value chains (GVCs).
gt_risks.mitigation: Develop and deploy engagement/communication strategies pre-implementation via GFPP plus ongoing TA; establish a dedicated project implementation team within NAFIN with clear roles/responsibilities; formalize PFI participation through legal agreements defining reporting obligations and performance expectations; proactive NAFIN/WB engagement with anchor companies to encourage supplier-firm participation.

gt_risks.description: Risk that SMEs, mid-caps, and participating financial institutions may not take up the new SLL/GL products at the expected pace or scale, given evolving global sustainability policies, limited familiarity with the instruments, and possible overestimation of market demand.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN business-development efforts for sustainable finance; targeted awareness and capacity-building for potential borrowers; TA to help beneficiary enterprises prepare Sustainability Plans and green investment proposals; monitor product uptake with scope to adjust instrument design/eligibility criteria, subject to Bank approval.
